original_question: Over a field k of positive characteristic, classify all regular injections of the affine line A^1_k into the affine plane A^2_k.
target_in_paper: Section 1, specifically Conjecture 1.1 as sharpened by Proposition 1.2 and partially supported by Theorem 1.3: the positive-characteristic analogue of the Abhyankar-Moh problem for affine-line embeddings in the affine plane, stated up to equivalence rather than as a vague free-form classification. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9506006))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient varieties A^1_k and A^2_k, the positive-characteristic setting, and the fact that the paper is after a classification problem rather than a single existence or uniqueness statement. It is also pointed in the right direction of the positive-characteristic failure of the characteristic-0 Abhyankar-Moh-Suzuki theorem. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1994-1995__37__295_0.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works in the setting of a field k of characteristic p>0, and the intended formulation is not just 'classify' but 'classify up to equivalence' under ambient automorphisms (and, on the source side, reparametrization of A^1 if the map formulation is used).

The paper-faithful object is a polynomial embedding / embedded affine line, i.e. a pair f,g in k[t] with k[f,g]=k[t], or equivalently a polynomial F in k[x,y] with k[x,y]/(F) isomorphic to k[t]; your draft says 'regular injections', which is broader and leaves open whether merely set-theoretic injectivity is intended.
The conjecture is formulated as a precise positive-characteristic replacement for the Abhyankar-Moh theorem, not as an unconstrained classification of arbitrary maps A^1_k to A^2_k.
The official nearby discussion includes an equivalent reformulation (Proposition 1.2), so the stand-alone question should indicate which notion of equivalence/classification is meant.
The draft omits the coordinate-ring formulation that the paper treats as equivalent and that is needed to make the problem self-contained for algebraic-geometry readers.

The draft does not signal that Theorem 1.3 is only a partial result toward the conjectural classification, which is part of the paper's framing of the problem. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1994-1995__37__295_0.pdf))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0. Classify, up to composition with automorphisms of A^1_k and A^2_k, all polynomial embeddings φ:A^1_k↪A^2_k; equivalently, determine the positive-characteristic analogue of the Abhyankar-Moh-Suzuki theorem for embedded affine lines in the affine plane. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1994-1995__37__295_0.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently (as in Proposition 1.2), classify up to Aut_k(k[x,y]) all polynomials F in k[x,y] such that k[x,y]/(F) is isomorphic to k[t]. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1994-1995__37__295_0.pdf))
justification: The nearest paper-faithful target is not the broad phrase 'classify all regular injections' but the Section 1 conjectural classification of embedded copies of the affine line in the affine plane in characteristic p>0, stated up to equivalence. The nearby Proposition 1.2 supplies the equivalent coordinate-ring formulation, while Theorem 1.3 gives only a partial result, so the paper's actual intent is a sharply framed normal-form/equivalence problem rather than an unrestricted classification of arbitrary injective morphisms. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9506006))
